name: Pride and Joy
reference: Pride and Joy (126 BPM shuffle, Eb): Stevie Ray Vaughan and Double Trouble, Texas Flood (1983; cut Nov 24 1982 at Jackson Browne's Down Town Studio, LA, eng. Richard Mullen, mixed by Lincoln Clapp)
rig: 'Number One' Strat (1962 body, 1963 neck, '59 pickup; .013-.058 strings, tuned down a half step) -> Ibanez Tube Screamer (the only effect: Drive off or low, Level full, Tone 12-3 o'clock) -> two Fender Vibroverbs (15-inch) plus Jackson Browne's 150 W Dumble ('Dumbleland') into a 4x12; one SM57 on a Vibroverb and one on the Dumble cab, 3-4 in off at ~45 degrees. Mullen: 'his sound came from a combination of the Fender and Dumble amps'. Ambience at the mix: an EMT plate.
notes: The documented blend as a dual rig: left a Vibroverb (Slammin's blackface Vibroverb, vibrato channel at his 'SRV' setting, into a JBL E130 Vibroverb IR: no Altec 15 IR is in the catalog), right a Dumble (the catalog's Steel String Singer #002 stands in for Browne's Dumbleland, which nobody captured), panned 20/80. Which amp carries this song is undocumented. Tube Screamer: TS9 (Craig Hopkins: the TS9 replaced the 808 in 1982 and the 808 never went to the studio; Vintage Guitar says 808: contested), at Hopkins' Drive 0 / Tone 6 / Level 10, on at load; SW8 takes it off. Strat voicing (the humbucker -> single-coil curve) in front of both amps; the right chain's amp is its end block, so tone.csv EQ cells can't reach it (tune it in the JSON). SW9 = a quarter-note echo at 126 BPM, not on the record. SW7 VIBE = the Vibratone (Leslie) of Cold Shot, slow rotor, half mixed: not on this song. Tune down a half step for Eb. Levelled offline with rigsim --exact to -14 LUFS (experiments D28).

left.label: Ibanez TS9, Drive 0 Tone 6 Level 10 (SRV's Tube Screamer as a boost: on at load, SW8 takes it off)
Fender Vibroverb blackface, vibrato channel V5, Slammin's SRV setting (DI)
Quarter-note echo 476 ms at 126 BPM (not on the record)

right.label: Quarter-note echo 476 ms at 126 BPM (not on the record)

vibe.note: Not on Pride and Joy: SRV's Fender Vibratone (Leslie) on Cold Shot / Couldn't Stand the Weather, slow rotor, low in the mix; a phaser approximates the rotor (no Doppler or horn)
